lastCompletedStory.title: WARNING: The log path is interpolated unquoted throughout the cap snippet

openQuestions: CAM-513 (flaky-test-isolation, filed on main from US-R1-003) remains open and unrelated to this story's diff.
nextStoryContext: US-R2-006 closed the reviewer's WARNING that buildConfigLogCapCommand (src/commands/setup.ts) left every ${logPathExpr} path expansion unquoted throughout the cap snippet (cat ${LOG}.chunk >> ${LOG}, tail -c N ${LOG} > ${LOG}.tmp, mv ${LOG}.tmp ${LOG}, rm -f ${LOG}.chunk ${LOG}.lock), and the v|V case arm's trailing `tail -f ${CAM_CONFIG_LOG}` in buildSetupMenuScript was unquoted too, while the sibling buildConfigLogCleanupCommand already quoted every expansion ("$CAM_CONFIG_LOG"). Since logPathExpr derives from ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} (configLogDirExpr), a TMPDIR containing a space word-splits the unquoted calls, silently sending the writer's cat/tail/mv/rm at the wrong path. NOTE for the next implementer: this story's implementation was found ALREADY PRESENT, complete and uncommitted, in the working tree at session start (a prior interrupted worker attempt never committed); this session's job was to review, verify, and finish it rather than write it from scratch -- verified the diff carefully against the story's acceptance description before trusting it. Fix: every path expansion in buildConfigLogCapCommand is now double-quoted ("${logPathExpr}", "${chunkPathExpr}", "${lockPathExpr}", a new "${tmpPathExpr}" const replacing the old bare ${logPathExpr}.tmp inline expansions), matching buildConfigLogCleanupCommand's convention. The sole deliberate exception is the outer $(wc -c < "${logPathExpr}") substitution wrapper itself, left unquoted (only the LOG path INSIDE it is quoted): wc -c's stdout is always a single numeric token, so IFS-splitting it is safe. Quoting reintroduces the exact literal-"-corrupts-the-outer-argument hazard buildConfigLogCapCommand's original zero-quote convention existed to avoid (its return value is spliced verbatim into the OUTER menu script's own double-quoted "tmux pipe-pane ... -o '...'" split-window argument, see the US-R2-004 patterns.md bullet for the full three-level quoting trace): a literal " reaching that argument unescaped closes it early and corrupts the generated script. Added a new sibling helper, escapeDoubleQuotesForOuterEmbed(snippet) (escapes every " to \", mirroring deferCommandSubstitution's $( -> \$( shape exactly), and the v|V arm now runs the cap command's output through BOTH helpers before splicing it in (escapeDoubleQuotesForOuterEmbed(deferCommandSubstitution(buildConfigLogCapCommand(...)))), plus quotes its own trailing tail -f "${CAM_CONFIG_LOG}". test/setup-config-log.test.ts's structural guard flipped from expect(command).not.toContain('"') to expect(command).toContain('"') (direct-bash-spawn callers see the real, already-quoted bash and never cross the escaping layer). Added a new real-tmux integration test in test/integration/setup-menu-viewer-live.test.ts (mirroring the US-R2-004 convention) that sets TMPDIR to a path containing a literal space, drives the v|V viewer through a real burst, and confirms the log lands at the correctly-quoted nested path with no stray 'has'/'space' siblings scattered in the parent scratch dir (the word-split failure mode this story closes). Full bun test 6110 pass / 0 fail (+1 from the new test), typecheck 0 errors, full bun run check:all spine green after one justified gate resolution: file-size-budget.json raised for src/commands/setup.ts (1223->1268, the new escapeDoubleQuotesForOuterEmbed helper plus its doc comment, the tmpPathExpr const, and the substantially-expanded quoting-rationale doc comments on buildConfigLogCapCommand), dated note prepended to _ref naming this story/CAM-510 and staged in the same commit. No knip/jscpd/coverage changes needed; no vendor/templates changes, no embed-vendor needed. Step 5.5: this story is a pure bash-quoting fix with no external library touched (no npm/bun package involved), recorded as no_external_lib_touched. scripts/cam/prd.json was left untouched/uncommitted by this story, per the AGENT.md rule that the implementer never edits prd.json.
